what: Which OF3T comparisons are FRAME-MATCHED and which are not, in one place. Every number below is read from of3t-apbback's REFAUDIT.json; nothing here is recomputed or new.
why: The campaign carried `the trunk is 5.41x upstream's own bf16` as its largest open defect. That ratio pairs a numerator scored against the MODEL float64 with a denominator that is upstream's bf16 against the MODEL float64 -- but our arm is CAPTURE-DRIVEN and upstream's is a FULL-MODEL run, so the two sides do not share a frame. Scored in one frame the same device tensors read 0.9565x. See D186.

frame_matched.comparison: our device arm and the floor BOTH scored against REF_LOCAL_f64, the capture's own float64

cross_frame.comparison: our CAPTURE-driven arm against the MODEL-frame floor. This is the campaign's 5.41x
cross_frame.reading: 5.4144x -- and it is measuring the frame
cross_frame.note: the floor 0.3147698294 is exactly the A26 denominator the campaign quotes, so the bar is the MODEL-frame floor and it has been paired with a LOCAL-frame numerator

the_same_tensors_twice: apbgrad_scope_RENORM_c64 and padshape_RENORM_w64 give identical readings to ten digits against both references (0.3833065668 and 1.7043040668). They are the same device tensors; the 4.45x between the two rows' published figures is the reference alone.
what_is_still_missing: The frame-matched comparison exists at CROP 64 only. REF_LOCAL_f64 and REF_LOCAL_bf16 are both c64 dumps. GRADIENTS' clause reads model scope at crop 384, where our arm is still capture-driven and upstream's bf16 arm is full-model, so that clause remains CROSS-FRAME. Closing it needs upstream 0.4.3 run from the SAME capture at crop 384, in float64 and in bf16 autocast -- upstream's own code from a saved boundary, CPU work, no card.
